finding.claim: The attacker-supplied iconUrl is stored without any validation. The nightly sync job later issues a server-side GET to it. An attacker can point it at internal services, cloud metadata (http://169.254.169.254/), or localhost. Any non-HTTP scheme the client doesn't support would simply fail. The HTTP client is the Java default, which does not follow redirects. The response body is read as a byte array, which gives some potential for data exfiltration or blind probing.

trace.note: update(webhook, icon) receives the attacker-controlled icon from PUT /profile
this.iconUrl = icon, stored with no scheme, host, or IP validation
sync() builds the request with URI.create(iconUrl) and sends a GET from the server

finding.guards_checked: The only validation in update() is the regex on `webhook` (line 12). It does not cover `icon`. There is no scheme, host allowlist, private-IP or DNS-rebinding check anywhere on the path. No egress proxy or other control is visible in this code.

verdict.reason: src/Profile.java:16 stores the unvalidated icon (the regex at :12 only checks webhook), and src/Profile.java:23 sends a server-side GET to URI.create(iconUrl) with no scheme, host, or IP restriction, so the attacker controls the target.
